column1: # Accountants & Co: text library for the cmui profit and loss report. KEY<TAB>TEXT; same KEY = variants picked by club id.

column2: {club} closes the period with a surplus of {result} on income of {income}, and the bank is in credit. These are, by any measure, a sound set of accounts.
A strong year: income of {income_m} has yielded a surplus of {result_m}, a margin the board may regard with quiet satisfaction. The bank balance stands at {balance_m}.
We are pleased to report a surplus of {result} for the year to date and a bank balance in credit. Few clubs of our acquaintance are so fortunately placed.
The year shows a surplus of {result_m}, at least a tenth of income, with the bank in credit at {balance_m}. We have no material concerns to raise.
{club} has traded at a modest surplus of {result} for the year, and the bank remains in credit. The margin is narrow but honest.
The year to date shows a surplus of {result_m} on income of {income_m}. It is a slim margin, and the board will wish to guard it.
Income has covered expenditure with a little to spare: a surplus of {result} and a bank balance of {balance}. Respectable, if not yet comfortable.
We report a small surplus of {result_m} and a positive bank balance. A modest result, but the club is paying its way, which is more than many can say.
The year shows a surplus of {result}, yet the bank account remains overdrawn at {balance}. The club is climbing out of its hole; it is not yet out of it.
A surplus of {result_m} this year is welcome news, though a bank balance of {balance_m} reminds us that earlier shortfalls have yet to be made good.
{club} is trading at a surplus of {result}, and the overdraft should narrow if this continues. We counsel patience rather than celebration.
We note with approval a surplus of {result_m} for the year. The balance, at {balance_m}, remains below zero, and the board should treat this surplus as repayment, not spending money.
The year shows a deficit of {result}, met for now from the club's reserves; the bank balance stands at {balance}. Reserves, we would observe, are spent only once.
{club} has incurred a deficit of {result_m} this year. The bank remains in credit at {balance_m}, but it is being drawn down to pay for it.
Expenditure of {expenditure} has exceeded income of {income}, leaving a deficit of {result}. The balance is still positive; the trend is not one we would wish to see continue.
A deficit of {result_m} has been absorbed by the club's cash at bank, which stands at {balance_m}. We recommend the board consider how long that cushion is to last.
The year shows a deficit of {result} and the bank account is overdrawn at {balance}. The board will wish to give these figures its early attention.
{club} is spending more than it earns, with a deficit of {result_m} for the year and a bank balance of {balance_m}. There is no cushion left to absorb further losses.
Expenditure of {expenditure} against income of {income} leaves a deficit of {result}, funded by an overdraft. We note that a bank's patience is not unlimited.
A deficit of {result_m} on the year and a bank balance of {balance_m}. We would be failing in our duty were we not to describe the position as unsatisfactory.

The year shows a deficit of {result} on income of only {income}, and the club is overdrawn at {balance}. In our professional opinion the position is serious and calls for immediate action by the board.
We must report plainly: a deficit of {result_m} against income of {income_m}, with no cash at bank to meet it. The club's standing as a going concern must now be the board's first consideration.

Expenditure has exceeded income by {result}, more than a quarter of everything the club earned, and the bank balance stands at {balance}. We draw the board's attention to the matter in the strongest terms.
These accounts disclose a deficit of {result_m} and a bank balance of {balance_m}. We regret that we must ask the board to treat the club's finances as its first and most pressing concern.
Wages absorbed {wages_pct}% of income this year. At this level, very little remains for anything else the club may need.
The wage bill of {wages_m} takes {wages_pct}% of income. We would gently remind the board that players are paid whether or not the gates hold up.
Wages stand at {wages_pct}% of income, a ratio we regard as unsustainable for more than a season or two. New contracts should be negotiated with this in mind.
We note that wages of {wages} consume {wages_pct}% of everything the club earns. The manager may wish to know this before offering his next contract.
Wages took a modest {wages_pct}% of income this year, well within prudent limits.
The wage bill of {wages_m} represents {wages_pct}% of income. The board has kept a firm hand on contracts, and it shows.
At {wages_pct}% of income, wages are comfortably under control. There is room, should the manager make a sound case, for a carefully chosen addition to the squad.
Wages absorbed {wages_pct}% of income this year, against {wages_pct_last}% last year. A welcome improvement.
The wage ratio has fallen from {wages_pct_last}% of income last year to {wages_pct}% this year. We commend whoever is responsible.
Wages now take {wages_pct}% of income, down from {wages_pct_last}% a year ago. The board should resist any temptation to give the gain straight back.
Wages absorbed {wages_pct}% of income this year, against {wages_pct_last}% last year. The trend merits watching.
The wage ratio has risen from {wages_pct_last}% of income last year to {wages_pct}% this year. Pay is growing faster than the club's earnings.
Wages now take {wages_pct}% of income, up from {wages_pct_last}% a year ago. We would ask that each new contract be weighed against this figure.
Player sales of {sales_m} made up {sales_pct}% of this year's income. Excluding sales, the year would show a result of {profit_ex_sales_m}.

The club has relied on the transfer market for {sales_pct}% of its income, some {sales_m} in all. Excluding sales the year would show a result of {profit_ex_sales_m}, the truer measure of everyday trading.
We note that {sales_pct}% of income came from selling players. A squad can be sold only once; excluding sales, the year would show a result of {profit_ex_sales_m}.
Player sales brought in {sales_m}, {sales_pct}% of the year's income. Excluding sales the year would show a result of {profit_ex_sales_m}; the board should not budget on another such year.
No players were sold this year; all of the income was earned from the club's ordinary football business.
The club has made no player sales this year, so the figures above reflect its everyday trading alone.
Players bought account for {bought_m}, or {bought_pct}% of expenditure. The board will wish to see that investment repaid on the pitch.
Transfer spending of {bought} made up {bought_pct}% of the year's expenditure. We take it the manager has his reasons.
Purchases of players took {bought_pct}% of expenditure this year, some {bought_m} in all. Such outlays are best judged by results, and in time by resale value.
Season tickets provided {tickets_pct}% of income, a loyal and dependable base for which the supporters deserve the board's thanks.
Season ticket sales made up {tickets_pct}% of income. Money paid in advance is the best kind, and the club is fortunate in its supporters.
At {tickets_pct}% of income, season tickets give the club a steady foundation. We advise against testing that loyalty with sharp rises in price.
The month shows a result of {month_result}, against {month_result_last} last month. A move in the right direction.
This month's result of {month_result} improves on last month's {month_result_last}.
Trading has improved month on month: {month_result} this month, compared with {month_result_last} last month. One month is not a trend, but it is a start.
The month shows a result of {month_result}, against {month_result_last} last month. A step back, which we trust is temporary.
This month's result of {month_result} falls short of last month's {month_result_last}. Monthly figures move with the fixture list, but the board should keep an eye on it.
Trading weakened month on month: {month_result} this month, compared with {month_result_last} last month. We shall comment further should the pattern repeat.
Transfer funds stand at {funds}. Any new signing would have to be paid for by a sale first.
The manager has no transfer funds at his disposal ({funds}). We would advise the board not to sanction purchases until this changes.
With transfer funds at {funds}, the club is not in a position to buy. The manager will need to work with the squad he has, or sell before he buys.
Transfer funds of {funds} are available. We advise that they be spent on need rather than reputation, and that wages be counted alongside the fee.
The manager has {funds} to spend. A fee is paid once; a contract is paid every week, and the board should weigh both.
Transfer funds stand at {funds}. Money left unspent is not wasted, and we would not regard it as a failure if some of it remained at the year end.
The club is overdrawn, with a bank balance of {balance}. We advise the board to hold off new signing-on fees until the balance improves.
With the bank balance at {balance}, we recommend that no new long contracts be agreed until the overdraft is reduced.
The account stands at {balance}. The board may wish to consider a sale or two, or a word with the chairman, before the bank raises the matter itself.
We note the bank balance of {balance}. Interest on an overdraft buys no points, and we urge the board to make its reduction a priority.
Cash reserves of {balance_m} give the club a sound cushion against a poor season.
The bank balance of {balance_m} is a credit to the board's stewardship. Reserves of this kind are best kept for the day they are needed.
With {balance_m} at bank, the club is well provided for. We would counsel against letting a healthy balance become an argument for loose spending.
Basis of preparation: compiled from the club's records without audit. Figures may differ by a small sum through rounding, and from the game's own screens in small particulars.
Basis of preparation: these management accounts are unaudited and drawn from the club's own books. Rounding may cause small differences, and the game's own finance screens may differ slightly.
Basis of preparation: unaudited; compiled from information supplied by the club. Totals may not cast exactly through rounding, and minor differences from the game's own screens are to be expected.

Basis of preparation: compiled without audit from the club's records as they stood on {date}. Amounts are rounded, so a small sum may go astray; the game's own screens may show slightly different figures.
We are, as ever, at the board's disposal.
We should be pleased to discuss these accounts with the chairman at his earliest convenience.
Should the board require any further explanation, we remain entirely at its service.
We thank the club's staff for their kind assistance and look forward to the next set of figures.
Marcus Hartwell FCA|M. Hartwell
Priya Raman ACA|P. Raman
Oluwaseun Adeyemi FCA|O. Adeyemi
Margaret Lindqvist FCCA|M. Lindqvist
